chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from a man, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The meaning of the hadith: The one who doubts in Allah after his birth, being upon the natural disposition (fitrah), would not incline to any good ever.
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of doubting Allah despite having a natural disposition to believe?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links persistent doubt (shakk) to a deviation from the primordial covenant (mithaq) inherent in human fitrah, suggesting that such doubt severs the soul from divine guidance. This highlights the Shia view that faith is not merely acquired but rediscovered, and failure to align with this innate nature results in a permanent spiritual misalignment.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Usman Bin Isa, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who doubts in Allah<sup>azwj</sup> after his birth being upon the nature (natural disposition to believe in Allah<sup>azwj</sup>), would not end up to anything good, ever!’
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from a man from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
One who doubts in Allah after being born from Muslim parents, forever, will not end up to anything good.’”
